title: The Singing Country Rendered as Schematic

features.name: song-paths rendered as fence-rows
features.desc-on-touch: The country has been mapped as a schematic: every song-line becomes a row, every singing-place marked as intersection. The fences are not barriers; they are notation. The country has taught you to read its own melody in the geometry of its human borders.

features.name: trees marking the intervals between notes
features.desc-on-touch: Each tree stands exactly where it should be in the song's measure. The spacing is not random; it is acoustic. The schematic describes not just where to sing, but how the land itself is organized by the intervals between utterances. The trees are resting-places for the voice.

features.name: the grid that learned to sing
features.desc-on-touch: Coordinates and coordinate lines, but now they hum. The schematic is not static; it breathes. Each cell in the grid has developed a frequency. Standing anywhere in the country, you are standing in a note. The entire landscape is a chord held in suspension.

features.name: voices tracking the song-paths
features.desc-on-touch: Someone is walking the schematic aloud, following each marked route and singing at the marked points. Their voice enters the country; the country receives it back, transformed. Each singer adds a variant; the schematic learns new harmonies from each passage.

inscription: the singing taught the country how to be arranged; the schematic taught the singing how to move through space

file.name: SongMaps_Country_Schematic_Tracings.txt
file.note: Coordinate-based descriptions of song-paths through regional NSW. Each verse is indexed to latitude/longitude. Each line is rendered as a map fence. Corruption: some song-paths lead to coordinates fro
